verdict.rationale: Vercel versions, reviews, and rolls back whatever it deploys, which includes code-defined automations such as Vercel Workflows. It deploys on every Git push with a preview URL per branch, supports team comments on previews, offers gradual rollouts, and can revert production to a previous deployment without a rebuild. None of this is documented as automation-specific; it is deployment-level lifecycle tooling that only covers automations when they are deployed as code. Missing for 10: automation-specific version history, review/approval flow for workflow changes, per-automation rollback docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Connect GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket to deploy on every push, with a preview URL for every branch.
Let teams and invited collaborators comment on your preview and production environments.
Revert production to a previous deployment without a rebuild when something breaks.
Send a new deployment to a percentage of traffic first, then promote it or roll back.
Vercel Workflows runs multi-step logic as durable code that can retry failed steps, wait for external events, and resume across crashes and deployments.
